observed_facts: Both affected raw claims use the identical address tuple: FISHER_CC9, word 1070, bit 3.
The source rows are distinct: Conveyor.asc rows 888 and 1412, with distinct IO names and descriptions.
Configio word 1070 has Low bank 144 with description 1794-IB16-211. The independently derived rack evidence identifies an input 1794-IB16 module with input bank 144.
The High half of word 1070 is bank 145 and has no hardware-bank match.

One-sided binding is established elsewhere: traces for words 100 and 101 accept their Low-bank matches and reject their unmatched High halves. An unmatched High half must not be used to select another module or an owner.
candidate_rule_description: When two or more raw physical claims share the same machine, Configio word, and bit, and independent directional bank/catalog evidence establishes one hardware context, preserve that context for investigation but do not select an owning claim. Mark every claim in the collision group REVIEW_REQUIRED.

preconditions: At least two distinct claim IDs share an identical machine, word, and bit.
An exact directional bank match and catalog-compatible module context is independently established.
No authoritative source specifies ownership precedence for the colliding claims.

proposed_transformation: Group raw physical claims by machine, word, and bit before selecting an owner.
Use only exact directional bank and catalog-compatible evidence to establish the shared hardware context.
When group cardinality exceeds one, retain every claim and set each disposition to REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Do not select an owner using IO name, description, source-row order, or an unmatched opposite LoHi half.
Do not cross-bind an unmatched High half to a Low-side module.

supporting_examples.evidence: Both claims collide on the same raw tuple. Word 1070 Low bank 144 has an exact compatible input-bank match for 1794-IB16; the source supplies no ownership-precedence fact.

counterexamples.observation: Low bank 130 is accepted while High bank 131 has no bank match. The accepted module is output-directional, demonstrating that unmatched High halves are not inferred as a second binding.
Low bank 132 is accepted while High bank 133 has no bank match, independently repeating the one-sided binding shape.
High bank 145 has no bank match; it cannot establish an alternative module context or resolve ownership between the two colliding claims.

ambiguities: This cluster contains only one duplicate address tuple, so it supports a narrow collision-preservation rule, not a general semantic ownership-precedence rule.
Neither raw claim name nor description is authoritative evidence that one claim should supersede the other.
additional_evidence_needed: Verified Fortna design documentation or another authoritative source defining ownership precedence for duplicate machine/word/bit claims, if a single owner must be selected.
tests_required: Group all physical claims by machine, word, and bit before any ownership decision.
Verify both word-1070 bit-3 claims remain REVIEW_REQUIRED and that no winner is emitted.
Regression-test words 100 and 101 to ensure unmatched High halves are not cross-bound.
Reject implementations that select an owner using source ordering, IO name, or description.

confidence.basis: The address collision is direct raw-source evidence. The Low-bank hardware context is independently corroborated by Configio, rack-module, and aggregate bank-map evidence. No evidence establishes an ownership-precedence convention.
